museum-guide.text: The river flood of 1911 filled the lower galleries to the height of a hand rail. The great gallery clock stopped at 4:52 in the morning and was rebuilt over the following two years.
The tall regulator clock in the entrance hall keeps the building's time. Its pendulum is compensated with mercury, and it chimes only on the hour.
The museum was founded by a watchmakers' guild that met in the same building for sixty years before it opened to the public.
The instrument room holds a brass orrery, two marine chronometers and a set of tuning forks used to check church bells across the province.
